sections.title: Performance Analysis — Canon
sections.content: The codebase is mid-build (per `AGENTS.md`'s phased plan), so several categories are thin because the code doesn't exist yet (engine's blocking/detect/agent modules are `NotImplementedError` stubs for Phase 2/3). I've reported honestly where that's the case rather than inventing issues.

sections.title: 1. N+1 queries
2. Unnecessary React re-renders
3. Caching opportunities
sections.content:
The big one is real but **not a bug yet** — it's a documented gap: `engine/agent/prompts.py:1-6` correctly identifies the ruleset block as the prompt-cache prefix ("the single largest cost lever"), but `build_ruleset_block`/`build_conflict_block` are `NotImplementedError("Phase 3")`. When implemented, use `cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}` on the ruleset block per AGENTS.md's Model Selection section — worth flagging now so it isn't missed when `agent/graph.py` gets built out.

No other caching gaps: TanStack Query is correctly scoped to only the run-status poll (`query-provider.tsx`), everything else is Server Components reading Postgres directly with no redundant repeated reads found.

sections.title: 4. Memory leaks
sections.content: None found. `web/lib/db/index.ts:24` caches the pg connection on `globalThis` to survive Next.js HMR. All `useEffect` intervals/listeners clean up correctly (`run-live.tsx:101` clears its interval, `conflict-queue.tsx:130` removes its keydown listener on unmount). The engine's FAISS/embedding concern is moot — `blocking.py` is entirely a stub, so there's no index or in-memory cache yet to leak.
